title: GrowWithHR Social Security Wave 5L Governed Family-Routing Catalogue

sourcePack.name: GrowWithHR generic Social Security controlled core snapshot
sourcePack.notes: All four records are existing exact controlled full files. Wave 5L adds no new source-file acquisition and routes only to chapter/source families; it does not determine applicability, contributions, benefits, cess, claims or remedies.

limitations: The Wave 5L catalogue remains needs-legal-review and is not a Social Security chapter applicability, scheme coverage, contribution, benefit, cess, claim, enforcement or remedy determination.

Only organisation-level family-route, core-source, First Schedule/chapter-routing, dedicated-family handoff, cross-family reconciliation, State/UT and escalation statuses plus controlled references are eligible for retrieval context.
Dedicated family reviews remain separate. Retrieval cannot substitute one family result for another or fill missing applicability facts.
BOCW Chapter VIII and unorganised/gig/platform-worker Chapter IX routes remain specialist-only in this wave.

chunks.title: Generic social-security First Schedule routing boundary
chunks.text: The Code ties the applicability of the chapters identified in the First Schedule to the corresponding schedule entries. Wave 5L records only whether a chapter/source-family route has been reviewed; it does not decide that any chapter applies to a customer, establishment or worker.

chunks.title: EPF, EPS and EDLI family handoff
chunks.sectionReference: Chapter III and related scheme framework
chunks.text: Chapter III provides the provident-fund family framework. Wave 5L may route a declared organisation-level issue to the dedicated EPF, EPS and EDLI reviews, but the generic route cannot decide establishment coverage, employee membership, wage ceilings, contribution rates, pension routing, insurance coverage or amounts.

chunks.title: ESI family handoff
chunks.text: Chapter IV provides the Employees State Insurance framework. Wave 5L may record that the ESI family requires dedicated review, but it cannot decide territorial coverage, employee insurance, wage ceilings, contribution rates, medical administration, benefits, exemptions, enforcement or individual entitlement.

chunks.title: Gratuity family handoff
chunks.text: Chapter V is the gratuity framework. The generic family router can hand the matter to the dedicated Gratuity source-readiness review but cannot classify an establishment, determine employee coverage, continuous service, wages, gratuity amount, nomination, forfeiture, claims or remedies.

chunks.title: Maternity Benefit family handoff
chunks.text: Chapter VI is the Maternity Benefit framework. Wave 5L records only a family-level handoff and does not decide establishment coverage, individual eligibility, benefit duration or amount, leave, nursing breaks, creche duties, employment protection, ESI overlap or any claim.

chunks.title: Employee's Compensation family handoff
chunks.text: Chapter VII is the Employee's Compensation framework. The generic route may direct the issue to the dedicated Chapter VII review but cannot classify a worker, decide ESI overlap, causation, injury, disease, disablement, dependency, liability, wages, compensation, claims or remedies.

chunks.title: BOCW social-security and cess specialist route
chunks.text: Chapter VIII addresses social security and cess for building and other construction workers. GrowWithHR has no approved substantive Chapter VIII family in this wave, so any BOCW route remains specialist-review only and cannot be converted into a coverage, cess, registration, benefit or worker-status conclusion.

chunks.title: Unorganised, gig and platform worker specialist route
chunks.text: Chapter IX addresses social security for unorganised workers, gig workers and platform workers. Wave 5L records only that a specialist Chapter IX route is required; it does not classify a person, aggregator, platform or employment relationship, or decide scheme registration, contribution, eligibility or benefit.

chunks.title: Current Central Rules routing context
chunks.text: The controlled 2026 Central Rules provide current procedural and chapter-specific rule context. Wave 5L uses them only to reconcile the declared source-family route and cannot use a generic rule reference to replace the dedicated EPF, ESI, Gratuity, Maternity Benefit or Employee's Compensation review.

chunks.title: Social Security Code commencement context
chunks.text: The controlled commencement notification is retained as effective-date and transition context for the Code. It does not by itself establish that a particular chapter, scheme, establishment, employee, worker or benefit route applies.

chunks.title: Commencement corrigendum context
chunks.text: The controlled corrigendum remains a companion commencement source. It must be reconciled with the principal notification and cannot independently select a social-security family, determine applicability or create an entitlement or contribution duty.

chunks.title: Cross-family and transition non-substitution boundary
chunks.text: The Code contains transitional, rule-making, schedule and repeal-and-savings provisions alongside separate chapter frameworks. Wave 5L cannot use one family result as a substitute for another, cannot resolve saved-law or State-transition questions automatically and cannot override any dedicated deterministic family review.
